text.p: These are the leading stories in Botswana's independent weekly newspapers The Guardian and Mmegi (The Reporter) on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Minister of local government Patrick Balopi is to make a statement on the newly introduced old-age pension scheme. There are fears that the first payments under the scheme, due to be made at the end of this month, will be delayed because of administration difficulties.

- The House of Chiefs has rejected the idea of a southern Africa free movement protocol. After a brefing by minister of home affairs Bahiti Temane, the chiefs said such a move would result in an influx of people into Botswana which would have a negative effect on the economy and, particularly, worsen the unemployment situation.

- During a panel discussion at the University of Botswana, opposition Botswana National Front (BNF) deputy leader Michael Dingake, said that if elected to power at the next elections in 1999, the BNF would not kow-tow to the international community.
